sections: Which uncertain choice is better? Suppose one action gives a reward of two every time, while another gives four with probability three quarters, and zero otherwise.
For the uncertain action, we multiply each possible reward by its probability, then add the results.
One quarter times zero, plus three quarters times four, gives an expected reward of three.
Three is greater than two. A decision maker maximizing expected immediate reward therefore prefers the uncertain action. This comparison is about averages, not a guarantee for any single trial.
